clue.text: The hard stuff's immaterial to them

definitions.meaning: strong liquor such as whisky or gin is called this
ghosts and souls are bodiless beings, so being immaterial is natural to them

explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are both distilled liquors and bodiless supernatural beings.

clue.text: Polish component a girl will put on the bill

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: a girl will contracts to she'll
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A girl buys an ingredient of furniture polish and charges it to her account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' matters in a down entry: the first piece sits on top of the second. 'a girl will' contracts to she'll, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin used as an ingredient in French polish and varnishes.

clue.text: The sort of courage endless ambition engenders

indicators.note: engenders means produces, so the letters of the two fodder words produce a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Boundless ambition breeds a certain kind of bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engenders' rearranges the fifteen letters of ENDLESS AMBITION.
explanation.definitionFit: It names unconquerable, unyielding bravery, a quality of spirit that cannot be subdued.

clue.text: Where I admit to a state of indebtedness

definitions.text: Where I admit to a state of indebtedness

parts.words: Where I admit to a state of indebtedness
parts.note: the place name, spoken, resembles someone confessing 'I owe a ...', while 'a state' points to one of the United States

explanation.definitionFit: It is a US state, and its name said quickly sounds like a confession of debt.

clue.text: Retains a mixture of solid fat

indicators.note: a mixture is a mixing up, so the letters of the word Retains are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hold of a blend of hardened fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is the solid glyceride component of animal and vegetable fats, used in candles.

clue.text: Proposition giving the alternative I object about

parts.note: OR introduces an alternative

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for I as object is read backwards

parts.note: ME is the object form of I

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a proposal that offers another option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' means the objective case of I; 'about' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement put forward to be proved, a proposition.

clue.text: The queen Titian represented with a tail!

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the painter's name is rearranged
the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the letter A added on as a tail at the end

explanation.surface: Titian painted a queen with a tail attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges TITIAN into TITANI, then 'with' attaches A as a tail. Titian was a Venetian painter, which makes 'represented' look like painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Island for which a Cockney may express hate

indicators.note: Cockney Londoners drop initial H, so the word is heard as they say it

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so hate comes out as 'ate

explanation.surface: A Londoner voices loathing for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner who drops the initial H; 'hate' becomes 'ate, which rhymes with the river-island word pronounced 'ait'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Unfortunate mishap whilst training

parts.note: training seems to mean practising, but means travelling by train, so the mishap is a crash on the rails

explanation.definitionFit: A crash or derailment is a mishap that happens while going by train.

clue.text: Might shape up as a hawthorn

parts.note: may is a verb meaning might
a tree is a shape that branches upward, as in a family-tree diagram

explanation.surface: Something could develop into a thorny bush.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the hawthorn's blossom, flowering in May, so the hawthorn is called this.

clue.text: Insurance with complications only women depict

indicators.note: complications tangle things, so the letters of the three fodder words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A complex insurance product is described by women alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with complications' rearranges the letters of ONLY WOMEN DEPICT.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment policy is a life-assurance plan paying a lump sum at maturity or death.

clue.text: An inexperienced skipper

parts.note: skipper suggests a ship's captain, but means a young animal that skips about in a field; inexperienced also suggests a naive person

explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep skips in spring, and the word also means an innocent, naive person.

clue.text: Regular companion the rabbit found about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the rabbit word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: cony is an old word for a rabbit

explanation.surface: A friend's pet rabbit turned up near the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close friend one spends time with habitually.

clue.text: Vessel you sound hesitant to identify

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the word as it is heard, spelt differently

parts.note: the word you, said out loud, matches how the opening letters of the jug word are pronounced
er is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone sounds unsure while trying to name a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' says YOU, which comes out spelt EW as in the jug word's pronunciation; ER is the hesitant noise. 'to identify' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a container for water.

clue.text: Suggesting the head of the house is slightly deranged?

definitions.text: Suggesting the head of the house is slightly deranged?

parts.words: Suggesting the head of the house is slightly deranged?
parts.note: the head of the house seems to be the householder, but is the roof, where a tile out of place is the idiom for mild madness

explanation.definitionFit: Having this is a British idiom for being a little mad; literally, a roof tile has come away.

clue.text: See 13
Tom with a chap of Spanish origin

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Alan is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A tomcat accompanies a man from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan describes something from Catalonia, a region of northeastern Spain.

clue.text: Could be annoyed but such a relief

indicators.note: could be means might be turned into, so the letters of annoyed are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone might be irritated, yet the outcome is soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkiller, something that brings relief.

clue.text: Not much in covering a natural home

indicators.note: in places the small-amount phrase inside the head covering

parts.note: a hat is a head covering
a bit means not much

explanation.surface: Barely anything covers an animal's home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the environment where a plant or animal naturally lives.

clue.text: Itinerant worker supported by Mr. Livingstone in Belgium

indicators.note: in a down clue being supported by means sitting on top of the other piece

parts.note: a hobo is a wandering worker
Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A tramp is backed by a London politician in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' puts HOBO above KEN. Ken Livingstone was a well-known London politician; Hoboken is a district of Antwerp.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoboken is a district of Antwerp, a place found in Belgium.

clue.text: Covering a theatrical weapon, perhaps

definitions.meaning: metal sheet wrapped round food is a covering
a stage sword could be a fencing foil made of cheap tin

explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet is used for wrapping, and a tin fencing sword would be a stage prop.

clue.text: Hammer, anvil or stirrup

parts.note: these look like a smithy's tools and tack, but are the three tiny bones of the middle ear

explanation.definitionFit: The malleus, incus and stapes are the small bones of the ear, each one called this.

clue.text: Cactus with which I put on a display

indicators.note: a display shows things set out afresh, so the letters of I put on a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener puts on a show of a prickly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges the letters of I PUT ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the genus of prickly-pear cacti.

clue.text: Was a model once, she reveals

definitions.note: a phrase for a person who reveals, standing for the noun

parts.note: ex means former, once
a poser is one who poses, as an artist's model does

explanation.surface: A woman who once modelled is telling secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposer is one who discloses or uncovers things.

clue.text: The end carriage

parts.note: this looks like the last coach of a train, but is the stand that carries a coffin at life's end

explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the frame on which a coffin is carried at a funeral.

clue.text: The punishment is nothing some Yorkshiremen tell you

indicators.note: Yorkshire speakers say nowt for nothing, and the word is heard as they say it

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A northerner says the penalty is nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire, a county in northern England, 'nowt' means nothing; the Russian whip word is pronounced the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a Russian whip used to flog criminals.

clue.text: Wet initially, one parliamentarian may be so described

definitions.text: Wet initially, one parliamentarian may be so described

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Wet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A drippy politician might be labelled this.
explanation.walkthrough: Wet is British slang for feeble, the same sense as the answer, so the whole clue defines as well as builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, ineffectual person is called a wet or a weakling.

clue.text: Beast to take on

definitions.meaning: to carry or shoulder a burden

explanation.definitionFit: It is a large animal, and as a verb means to carry or shoulder.

clue.text: The bust of one she married

parts.note: her is the possessive of she

explanation.surface: A sculpture of a woman's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A herm is a square pillar topped with a sculpted head, a bust on a pedestal.

clue.text: St. Peter's assignment for one in a Manx court?

definitions.meaning: Peter was given charge of the keys of heaven
the House of Keys is the Isle of Man's assembly, so one of its officers might bear this title

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man (Manx) has a parliament called Tynwald whose lower chamber is the House of Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: St Peter holds heaven's gates, and the title fits an official of the House of Keys.

clue.text: An opening under the bridge

parts.note: the bridge seems to span a river, but is the bridge of the nose, below which are the air passages

explanation.definitionFit: Each air passage of the nose opens below its bony ridge.

clue.text: It's made to measure current after lunch as well

definitions.text: It's made to measure current after lunch as well

parts.words: It's made to measure current after lunch as well
parts.note: made to measure suggests tailoring, but it is an instrument for electric current that works morning and afternoon alike

explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument that measures electric current in amperes.
